title: A tainted Cmd.Path is not evidence when it differs from Args[0]
claim: Only argv reaches the command sink callback. os.StartProcess executes lp/c.Path, so a tainted cmd.Path with a clean Args[0] runs an attacker-chosen binary without a report.
repro_command: cp .omo/review/evidence/sink-exec/review_sinkexec_test.go iast/os/exec/testapp/ && cd iast/os/exec/testapp && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go tool orchestrion go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestReview' . (output: .omo/review/evidence/sink-exec/go1.26.6-output.txt, .omo/review/evidence/sink-exec/go1.27.0-output.txt)

title: Windows SysProcAttr.CmdLine bypasses the argv evidence
claim: On Windows a non-empty attr.Sys.CmdLine replaces argv as the executed command line, but the sink inspects only argv, so a tainted CmdLine is not reported.

title: Existing tests miss the risky exec boundary cases
claim: No committed tests cover Path divergence, nil Args, Start twice, tainted Env/Dir, a canceled context, or multi-argument offset mapping.

title: Joined evidence does not show argument boundaries
claim: Argv is space-joined without quoting, so different argv shapes produce the same evidence. This matches other tracers.
repro_command: cp .omo/review/evidence/sink-exec/review_sinkexec_test.go iast/os/exec/testapp/ && cd iast/os/exec/testapp && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go tool orchestrion go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestReview' .

title: A tainted argv[0], or the command after sudo/doas, is emitted with its full source value
claim: The preserved command bytes are not sensitive, so a tainted executable and its whole source value are sent in clear unless the redaction patterns match. This is intended and matches Java.
